correctness.rationale: The exact conditional-hazard sum reduces to a symmetric signed two-exponential objective. A strictly increasing sinh(beta z)/sinh(alpha z) gives at most one derivative crossing on the half-horizon and fixes all global minima from its endpoint signs, including both equality cases. Monotone boundary functions give exact three horizon phases, and an analytic power series gives the universal square-root bifurcation. The included 7000-case standard-library checker (455000 grid comparisons) independently challenges the formulas, witness thresholds, and limiting results; finite checks are explicitly not the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior massed/spaced-input genetic circuit work has one intermediate activator and maximizes reporter-expression peaks under threshold gating, while Gaussian dephasing uses a different objective and stochastic kernel. These are substantively broader timing themes but do not state a result that dominates the signed two-memory three-event classification. The generic hyperbolic-sine monotonicity lemma is standard and is not asserted to be new.

value.rationale: Controlled repeated thermal stress is scientifically motivated by documented competing physiological acclimatization and sensitization. The complete three-geometry optimum, exact two threshold ratios, and universal splitting coefficient distinguish center-spacing from off-center and clustered regimes rather than merely computing one local derivative. It can serve as an analytically testable null benchmark for designing or interpreting controlled three-challenge protocols. It explicitly makes no field-calibrated or organism-universal prediction.
